newsitem.title: USA: Coastal earnings up more than 20 percent in quarter.
newsitem.headline: Coastal earnings up more than 20 percent in quarter.

text.p: Coastal Corp. Wednesday said its second-quarter earnings rose more than 20 percent to a record $79.3 million, or 70 cents per share, boosted largely by gains in its refining, marketing and chemicals business.

In the 1996 second quarter, the Houston-based energy holding company earned $54.1 million, or 47 cents a share, after a one-time charge of $12 million for the early redemption of high-cost debentures.
"We remain on track to exceed our 15-percent growth target for 1997, with stronger earnings, a stronger balance sheet and a proven strategy," said Coastal Chairman David Arledge.

Profits at Coastal's refining, marketing and chemicals segment nearly doubled to $42.7 million from $23.5 million in the 1996 second quarter, due to past investments and a restructuring of its refining and marketing businesses. Refining margins improved as expected, especially for refiners capable of refining heavy and sour crudes, it said.
Coastal's natural gas segment, the company's largest profit contributor, saw earnings rise to $94.3 million from $73.8 million, as results improved for both its regulated and unregulated operations.
Operating profits in exploration and production fell to $30.5 million from $41.0 million as a continued rise in natural gas production was offset by lower oil and gas prices.
Coastal's power operations reported earnings before interest and income taxes of $10.0 million, compared with $11.4 million for the same period last year.
Profits from coal tumbled to $6.3 million from $23.9 million after the sale of Coastal's Utah operations in the fourth quarter of 1996.
Coastal has consolidated assets of more than $11 billion.
Its stock fell 19 cents to $56.50 on the New York Stock Exchange in early afternoon trading.
